assessment.intent: The article clearly aims to give property-management companies a practical website structure that serves two distinct audiences: owners evaluating a manager and tenants needing fast support.
assessment.specificity: Strong. It names the exact page types, gives an owner-page outline, and separates sales, support, listings, portal links, and fee framing instead of relying on generic website advice.
assessment.evidence: Appropriate and restrained. The claims are mostly structural recommendations, with support from the BC OIPC PIPA guidance on minimum collection and the W3C WAI forms tutorial on accessible form design.
assessment.voice: Very close to Michael's target voice: direct, Canadian, constructive, owner-focused, and grounded in tradeoffs. It avoids corporate padding and gives useful opinions without pretending to be a guarantee.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The page-type table, sample owner page outline, and FAQ section make this a genuinely reusable planning asset for property managers rather than a thin blog post.
